title: MWAA: managed Airflow and the cost of leaving it idle

videos.script: Every data platform has a pipeline that must run at three in the morning, and something has to start it. {{clock}} Airflow is the tool most teams reach for. A pipeline is a Python file, and Airflow runs its tasks in order, retries them, and remembers every run. {{dag}} MWAA is Airflow run by AWS. You give it a bucket of DAG files, and AWS keeps the scheduler, the workers and the database running for you. {{parts}} Running is the word to hold on to. An environment cannot be paused. The smallest one costs about six hundred dollars a month, whether it works two hours a night or twenty. {{bill}} moto has no MWAA at all, and you will see the exact error, and why it names an address nobody typed. {{moto}} Then the same pipeline without Airflow: a Step Functions state machine, started by EventBridge Scheduler, which cost nothing while they wait. {{sfn}} By the end you will know which of the two a team should pay for, and when that answer changes. {{end}}
